    {id:"Q001",answer:"Taking Oathkeeper during Act does not make the Exile Usurper immediately.     {id:"Q006",answer:"At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among ties).     {id:"Q007",answer:"Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply: Chancellor/Exile to the space for warbands left in personal bank (Chancellor: 18+→6, 11–17→5, 4–10→4, 0–3→3; Exile: 9+→6, 4–8→5, 0–3→4), while Citizen goes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; (4) save unspent Supply by moving marker one extra space left per unused Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optionally resolve Rest powers, each once in chosen order.",support:"supported",evidence:"Rest mandatory order, steps 1–5."},
    {id:"Q008",answer:"Search costs 2 Supply from your region discard pile. Choose either source, never both. Draw 3 (fewer only if source runs out, a world Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw); do not voluntarily stop early. From the world deck, draw one at a time; when a Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track. If the source empties, take only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.",support:"supported",evidence:"Search section: costs and world-deck versus discard Vision handling."},
    {id:"Q009",answer:"Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle. Favor on the discarded card returns immediately to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.",support:"supported",evidence:"Discard destinations paragraph."},
    {id:"Q010",answer:"You may have up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. A true Vision can be revealed only by an Exile, faceup in its separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it does not use an adviser slot.     {id:"Q011",answer:"Both actions cost 1 Supply and require an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets already); relics and ruins are ineligible. Finite favor/warband sources limit gains to what's available; secrets are unlimited.",support:"supported",evidence:"Muster and Trade sections."},
    {id:"Q012",answer:"Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. You may instead Recover either banner from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. Flip it to normal side if Mob; there is no seizure penalty. For Darkest Secret, pay secrets strictly greater than its current amount; put the payment on it, the new holder takes 1 old secret, and previous holder takes the rest. From yourself, all old secrets return to you; from shared bank, the remainder stays there.",support:"supported",evidence:"Recover section and banner subrules."},
    {id:"Q013",answer:"To Recover another player's Darkest Secret, the suited card(s) at their pawn's site must match none of their faceup advisers. If there are no suited cards there (including an empty site or a ruin-only site), it is protected. A ruin has no suit and facedown advisers have no suit. If the holder has no faceup advisers but there is a suited site card, that card matches none of their advisers, so the Secret is recoverable. Recovering it from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.",support:"supported",evidence:"Corrected Darkest Secret protection rule: suited card at pawn's site matching none of faceup advisers; empty/ruin-only protects; no-adviser case recoverable."},
    {id:"Q014",answer:"Choose as defender any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one Campaign target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map (each gives 1 defense die). If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics there (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to banner resources), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice).     {id:"Q015",answer:"Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force; apply relevant modifiers. Oathkeeper gives +1 defense die and Usurper +2 when relevant. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie means defender wins.",support:"supported",evidence:"Campaign steps 2, 4–5."},
    {id:"Q016",answer:"After attacker victory, before targets, defender kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; resolve defeated plan effects.     {id:"Q017",answer:"When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any targeted site. Defender/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, but not other players' advisers; the player using a plan pays its cost and each plan is used by only one player. Declared defender chooses order/timing/priority for disagreements. Chancellor chooses which Imperial warbands die; surviving site garrisons return to Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizen board warbands stay. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.",support:"supported",evidence:"Campaign defender selection and Imperial defense paragraphs."},
    {id:"Q018",answer:"Base Travel costs (before modifiers): within Cradle 1; Cradle→Provinces 2; Cradle→Hinterland 4; Provinces→Cradle 2, within Provinces 2, Provinces→Hinterland 2; Hinterland→Cradle 4, Hinterland→Provinces 2, within Hinterland 3. Move to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. If the destination is facedown, reveal it and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and its printed relics facedown from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases; a Free Travel effect is the final override and makes Supply payment zero despite increases. Restrictions for entering a site still apply unless ignored. Site effects include Coast-to-Coast cost 1 and ignores Narrow Pass; Charming Valley adds 1 when traveling from it; Shrouded Wood costs 2 and ignores Narrow Pass/Hidden Place; Buried Giant lets you flip a board secret facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass; Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle free but adds 1 when traveling to Hinterland. Hidden Place requires flipping a board secret facedown to travel there; Narrow Pass requires entering via it when entering its region from another; Shrouded Wood may dictate destination if enemy-ruled.",support:"supported",evidence:"Travel cost table, cost-order paragraph, Travel modifiers and site-power bullets."},
    {id:"Q019",answer:"The Grand Scepter holder cannot use its powers on the turn they took it. On later turns, its holder (even an Exile) may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at the Reliquary. Acceptance converts the recipient to Citizen: flip board, replace their board and map warbands with purple (if purple is short, the new Citizen chooses which to remove/replace), discard revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, end their Act if it's their turn, and refresh Supply to full. Forced Citizenship powers use the same status conversion but require no Scepter offer, relic gift, or invented exchange; only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers a modifier.",support:"supported",evidence:"Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, and Forced Citizenship paragraphs."},
    {id:"Q020",answer:"Chronicle Oath: if winner won by Vision alone, next Oath matches that Vision; for any other or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one, and save the goal. If winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards (including boxed) to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; each acceptor must flip to Citizen and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle all remaining denizens in play (excluding cards retained at sites, Archive, and Dispossessed); top stack is 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions = 12 cards; middle is 15 denizens plus remaining 3 Visions = 18; remaining denizens go below.
